reference: Ernst Ising, Z. Phys. 31, 253 (1925); Lars Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944); Nicholas Metropolis, Arianna W. Rosenbluth, Marshall N. Rosenbluth, Augusta H. Teller and Edward Teller, J. Chem. Phys. 21, 1087 (1953). Ising solved the chain and found no transition. Onsager solved the square lattice exactly and found one at T_c = 2/ln(1+√2). The Metropolis algorithm samples the Boltzmann distribution by proposing single flips and accepting them with probability min(1, exp(−ΔE/T)). Here the lattice is updated as a checkerboard: two half-sweeps per step, each parity with its neighbors held fixed, so the GPU can flip every site of one color at once.
equation: E = −J Σ⟨ij⟩ sᵢsⱼ − h Σᵢ sᵢ,   P(flip) = min(1, e^{−ΔE/T}),   T_c = 2/ln(1+√2) ≈ 2.269
limitations: Complete evidence covers only the domain in validation/ISING.md: h = 0, uniform field shape, periodic square grids of 128 (and 192 for the Binder cumulant), equilibrium averages at T = 1.5, 1.8, 2.0, 2.1, 2.5 and 3.0, float32 spins on SwiftShader.
T_c agrees with Onsager at 0.13% through the Binder fixed-point estimator, which assumes the universal U* = 0.61069; the model-free crossing between grid sizes is inconclusive in quick mode.
Different seeds read windows of one hash sequence (tick0 below one million), so two seeds are independent only when their windows do not overlap; the tool allocates disjoint windows and records them.
Nonzero or patterned fields, non-square aspects, coarsening dynamics, critical exponents, the rgba16f fallback and the Magnetization, Domain walls and Bond energy views are not validated.
remaining: Run node tools/ising-science.js --full --write on a local machine for the model-free Binder crossing at L = 128, 192 and 256, T = 2.2 and 2.4 at L = 256, and three seeds per temperature.
Test the half-float fallback, nonzero and patterned fields and the other views.

numerical.scope: The actual ISING_STEP checkerboard Metropolis in the real studio at h = 0 on the periodic 128 x 128 grid: <|m|> against Yang at T = 1.5, 1.8, 2.0, 2.1 and u against Onsager at those and T = 2.5, 3.0; T_c from Binder cumulants at L = 128 and 192 reweighted around T0 = 2.27; the tab's own |m| series against the read-back.
numerical.criteria: Each comparison passes when the series is at least 50 tau_int long and |measured - exact| <= 3.5 standard errors (stats.seriesMean, Sokal window); a T_c estimate counts when its moving-block bootstrap error is below 0.005 and fails the run if it is then more than 3.5 errors from Onsager; the tab series must equal the read-back exactly; u(T_c) must equal -sqrt 2 within 1e-14.
numerical.benchmark: Yang, Phys. Rev. 85, 808 (1952): M = (1 - sinh(2/T)^-4)^(1/8). Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944): u(T) with the elliptic integral by the AGM, checked at T_c (u = -sqrt 2), against direct quadrature, against Onsager's double integral and against the low-temperature series; T_c = 2/ln(1 + sqrt 2) via the Binder crossing and the fixed point U* = 0.61069 (Kamieniarz and Bloete 1993; Salas and Sokal 2000). Temperatures count only where the exponential finite-size bound is below 1e-6.
numerical.failureControl: The same shader with acceptance exp(-dE/2T), and with the neighbor sum dropped from dE, injected into copies of the studio: both fail every magnetization and energy test they enter (|z| from 1212 to infinity).
numerical.limitations: h = 0, uniform field, periodic square grids, equilibrium averages, float32 on SwiftShader. The model-free Binder crossing is inconclusive in quick mode (L = 192 is shorter than 50 tau_int); T_c rests on the fixed-point estimator, which assumes the universal U*.

print.scope: Default plate (grid 256, T = 2.27, Spins view, Pixelate, graphite) after 500 sweeps: the module exportPNG at 2400 x 2400, Studio.exportData() and the shell print export at 8 in and 300 ppi.
print.criteria: Every unambiguous module PNG pixel carries the ink of the spin under its center (0 wrong of 5,607,424) and a one-cell displacement is detected; exported spins.npy and abs_m_series.npy identical to the read-back; every one of 65,536 cell centers in the shell sheet classified as its spin; spins, sweep count, series and recipe unchanged by all exports.
print.benchmark: The read-back float32 spin texture itself, independently mapped to print pixels.
print.failureControl: The spin field shifted by one cell must mismatch over 10% of the checked pixels (measured 19%).
print.limitations: Spins view only; the shell supersamples this tab because it does not declare fieldCells(), so sheet cell edges are blended and only cell centers are checked there.

domain.parameters: grid 128 x 128 (Binder also 192 x 192, print 256 x 256), aspect 1:1, h = 0, hMode uniform, T in {1.5, 1.8, 2.0, 2.1} from the Cold start and {2.5, 3.0} from the Hot start; Binder at T0 = 2.27 reweighted over 2.2628 to 2.2772; seeds and tick0 values in validation/results/ising-science.json.
domain.conditions: Periodic boundaries, J = k_B = 1; 1000 burn-in sweeps then 8000 (below T_c) or 6000 (above) measured; Binder 4000 + 40000 (L = 128) and 6000 + 28000 (L = 192) sweeps from Cold; running false, warmup 0, the tab's own step() and sample().
domain.resolution: Samples every 4 sweeps (Binder every 8 and 12); standard errors 3.6e-5 to 6.7e-4; T_c to 0.0030; print at 2400 x 2400 px (8 in at 300 ppi).
domain.precision: float32 (rgba32f) spin textures on SwiftShader, 24-bit uniform random numbers from the integer site hash, binary64 analysis in the page and in Node, RGBA8 print.
